results.content: # Title:Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain. View a PDF of the paper titled Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain, by Joanna Komorniczak. > Abstract:Concept drift is among the primary challenges faced by the data stream processing methods. This work presents the Frequency Filtering Metadescriptor -- a tool for characterizing the data stream that searches for the informative frequency components visible in the sample's feature vector. The presented solution is capable of generating a metadescription of the data stream, separating chunks into groups describing specific concepts on its basis, and visualizing the frequencies in the original spatial domain. The generalization in the frequency domain adapted in the proposed solution allows to capture the complex feature dependencies as a reduced number of frequency components, while maintaining the semantic meaning of data. |  | (or  arXiv:2502.04813v1 [cs.LG] for this version) |. results.content: This page provides the most accurate and concise summary worldwide for the paper titled Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain. ## [Literature Review] Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain. [# [Literature Review] Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain](/file? The paper titled "Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain" by Joanna Komorniczak addresses the issue of concept drift in data streams, which refers to the shifts in the underlying data distribution over time, affecting the performance of classifiers that rely on outdated information. The results indicated that ffm allows for competitive concept identification compared to PCA (Principal Component Analysis) and confirms its capability to effectively analyze high-dimensional data streams, particularly where traditional methods may struggle due to the curse of dimensionality. In summary, the Frequency Filtering Metadescriptor (ffm) showcases a robust approach to analyzing nonstationary data streams in the frequency domain, benefiting from the inherent generalization capabilities of frequency analysis.
